findings.title: Three scans that enforce two rules each have their second rule silently dropped from catalog/scans.toml and, for two of the three, from policy/RULES.toml's `check` field too
locations: src/Scans/api_page_structure.jl:1-3 — `# SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE — RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API, RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING` ... `no empty \`@docs\` block ... no \`@index\` block`
src/Scans/api_page_structure.jl:12-19 — the code that actually hits an empty `@docs` block and an `@index` block, both `RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING` clauses ('no `@index`, and no empty block')
catalog/scans.toml:177-182 — `rule = "RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API"` only, no second rule field

src/Scans/dead_ref.jl:1,6 — header names both rules; the regex `r"§\s?[0-9]|docs/(src|[A-Z]+\.md)|[A-Z]{4,}\.md|inspiration/"` includes `inspiration/`, the exact example `RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE` and its own ARCHITECTURE row cite
policy/RULES.toml:446-451 — `RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE` `check = ["panel"]`, never citing `scan:SCAN.DEAD_REF` even though a triage scan does catch its `inspiration/` case
policy/RULES.toml:432-437 and :425-430 — here `RULE.CIT.DOI` and `RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE` both correctly cite `scan:SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK` (this pair is NOT drifted)
findings.description: The claim 'which RULE.* id(s) does scan X enforce' has four homes: the scan file's own header comment (src/Scans/*.jl), the scan's actual code, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §12.B (the table catalog/scans.toml's own header comment calls its 'verbatim' source), and catalog/scans.toml's `rule` column, which policy/RULES.toml's `check` field is checked against. Three scans genuinely enforce two rules apiece (confirmed by reading their code, not just their comments: SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE's empty-`@docs`/`@index` checks are RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING clauses; SCAN.DEAD_REF's `inspiration/` pattern is RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE's own example of an inaccessible source). ARCHITECTURE.md §12.B lists both rules for all three. catalog/scans.toml's single `rule` field keeps only the first rule in every one of the three cases — the second is dropped in 3 of 3 multi-rule rows, which is a class, not one slip. For SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE and SCAN.DEAD_REF the drop propagates: policy/RULES.toml's `check` field for RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING and RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE also fails to cite the scan that does catch part of the violation, so RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE reads as `check = ["panel"]` (no automated check) when a triage scan in fact has a live regex for it. Only the DOI_CROSSCHECK pair escaped the propagation — RULES.toml is correct there, so only catalog/scans.toml is stale for that one. Ground truth (the scan code) sides with ARCHITECTURE.md §12.B and the scan headers; catalog/scans.toml and (for two rules) policy/RULES.toml are the drifted copies.
findings.resolution_hint: Either widen catalog/scans.toml's `rule` column to a list (matching the two-rule §12.B rows) and regenerate policy/RULES.toml's `check` fields from it, or, if the schema intentionally admits one canonical rule per scan, add the missing scan reference by hand to RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING's and RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE's `check` arrays in policy/RULES.toml so RULE_WITH_CHECK's own audit doesn't undercount them as `panel`/incomplete.
findings.contradicts: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2456,2460,2473 (§12.B) and the header comments of src/Scans/api_page_structure.jl, src/Scans/doi_crosscheck.jl and src/Scans/dead_ref.jl

findings.title: policy/RULES.toml's one-line statement for RULE.INST.CARRY drops one of the three real release-blocking conditions
locations: src/CLI/Release.jl:33-45 — `carry_release_fails`: "Three things do. A carried `blocker` or `major`... A finding carried `Passes.CARRY_LIMIT` times... And a backlog that has not fallen since the last release" — the docstring and the code (`serious`, `over`, backlog-vs-`hist` checks) implement exactly three conditions

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2409 — §12.A row: "...a final release refuses while a carried blocker or major stands, the backlog is not draining, or anything has been carried three times" (three conditions, matching the code)

policy/RULES.toml:575-576 — `RULE.INST.CARRY` `statement`: "...a final release refuses while a carried blocker or major stands or the backlog is not draining" (only two conditions — the CARRY_LIMIT/'carried three times' clause is missing)
findings.description: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §12.A states of its own table (§12.A intro, 'policy/RULES.toml records per id the file, the section, the one-line statement below') that this is the source of RULES.toml's `statement` field, so the same claim — what makes a final release refuse under RULE.INST.CARRY — has (at least) three homes: the actual gate `src/CLI/Release.jl:carry_release_fails`, the ARCHITECTURE.md §12.A summary, and policy/RULES.toml's regenerated `statement`. The code implements three refusal conditions (a carried blocker/major; a finding carried `CARRY_LIMIT` (3) times, which is 'no longer a deferral' and needs an owner ruling; a rising carry backlog), and ARCHITECTURE.md's row names all three. policy/RULES.toml's `statement` field names only two, omitting the CARRY_LIMIT/'carried three times' escalation path entirely — a reader of RULES.toml alone (which is what `LEG.SENTINELS`-adjacent tooling and any consumer skimming the rule register would read) would believe a minor/nit finding can be carried indefinitely as long as it isn't a blocker/major and the backlog is falling, which is false: `carry_release_fails` refuses release the moment any single id's carry count reaches 3, independent of severity or backlog trend. This is exactly the drift the lane looks for — a stale copy that lost a whole clause, not a rewording.
findings.resolution_hint: Regenerate policy/RULES.toml's `statement` for RULE.INST.CARRY (via `gbgdev rules`, per the file's own header instruction) so it names all three refusal conditions actually implemented by `carry_release_fails`, matching docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §12.A.
